source: Royal Government of Cambodia, General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), "ខែ្សសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំពោតនៅកម្ពុជា" (Corn Production Value Chain in Cambodia), 2017
text:
For background context, the source document notes that corn is one of the world's most important staple/feed crops, particularly in Africa, Asia, and the Americas. Globally, corn accounted for an estimated 765 million hectares of harvested area worldwide with world production of about 1,027 million tons in a recent year (per the source's cited figures from CGIAR, 2017 and Spurlock & Novak, 2017). The top 10 corn-producing countries accounted for roughly 851.1 million tons of that total. The United States was the largest single producer at 314-337.5 million tons (the source cites slightly different figures from different charts), followed by China at 224.9-227 million tons, Brazil (58.5 million tons), the EU-27 (73.6 million tons), India (23.4 million tons), Mexico (37.5 million tons), and smaller volumes from Indonesia, Egypt, Japan, and Canada. Corn provides an estimated 20% or more of daily dietary calories for people in 21 countries, and 30% or more in 12 countries with a combined population of around 310 million people.

This global context is included in the source as background for understanding Cambodia's position in regional and world corn trade, but is not itself Cambodia-specific agronomic or market guidance.
